rule: Each relation names a transformation of a verdict's inputs and the part of the verdict that must not change under it. The runner executes every declared relation over the whole corpus and fails on a relation it does not implement or implements without declaring, so this file and the runner cannot drift apart. The relations are metamorphic relations in the sense of Chen, Cheung and Yiu (1998): they check the checker without an oracle for the right answer, by comparing outputs across related inputs.

relations.name: claim_is_echoed
relations.invariant: verdict.claim equals the claim that was assessed, for every case and every scope

relations.name: scope_is_echoed_not_consulted
relations.invariant: verdict.scope equals the scope given (the default when none or empty is given), and status, reason and guidance are identical across every declared scope

relations.name: envelope_shape
relations.invariant: as_dict() carries exactly the envelope keys, decisive_if only when the status is not_established, missing_evidence as a list of strings and scope as a dict

relations.name: observation_key_order_is_irrelevant
relations.invariant: the observations in reversed insertion order give the same verdict

relations.name: unrelated_field_is_ignored
relations.invariant: an added observation field the checker does not read gives the same verdict

relations.name: assessment_is_deterministic
relations.invariant: assessing the same inputs twice gives equal verdicts

relations.name: inputs_are_not_mutated_or_aliased
relations.invariant: the observations and scope objects are unchanged after assessment, and changing the caller's scope object afterwards does not change the verdict's scope

relations.name: verdict_is_immutable
relations.invariant: assigning to a verdict field raises FrozenInstanceError

relations.name: state_comparison_is_symmetric
relations.invariant: swapping expected_state and observed_state gives the same status and reason

relations.name: acceptance_premise_flip_never_inverts_polarity
relations.invariant: setting one acceptance premise of a decisive case to false never yields the opposite decisive status (it may yield not_established or leave the verdict unchanged)

relations.name: canonical_separates_distinct_states_and_ignores_key_order
relations.invariant: every declared distinct pair has distinct canonical forms, and every mapping state value in the corpus has the same canonical form under any key order at any depth
